marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: FPIs turned net sellers, pulling out ₹35,860 crore from Indian equities in September
Rising crude oil prices and global rate hike concerns sparked capital outflows from emerging markets
En-masse selling by foreign investors wiped out trillions in market capitalization

whatHappening: Indian stock markets remain closed today for the weekend following the Gandhi Jayanti holiday on October 2
Benchmark shares posted their longest weekly losing run in 25 years, extending losses for an 8th consecutive week
In the last session, Sensex dropped over 570 points while Nifty slipped below the 22,300 mark
UPI transaction volume jumped 27% to touch 145 billion during the first half of the year
summary: In the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices suffered sharp losses, marking their longest weekly losing streak in 25 years amid relentless foreign portfolio investor outflows. Markets were closed on October 2 for Gandhi Jayanti and remain shut today for the weekend. Trading will reopen on Monday, 5 October.
